classification: assistant-written summary of owner requirements; not a transcript or quotation
purpose: Plain-language requirements for a developer building the ecommerce operating system. IDs preserve reference continuity without publishing original messages.

requirements.summary: Provide methodology reference for an ecommerce system focused on product research, finished ads and stores, campaign tests and improvement. Historical agents, code and schemas illustrate methods; they are not supplied working software or promised reusable components. Exclude private data.

The product is private and hosted, supports multiple brands/stores/accounts within one business, and includes a full database. Reconcile Downloads and prior work with emphasis on recent corrections. Deliver commercially credible ads and pages rather than generic AI output or unnecessary process terminology.

Begin with owner approval of creative direction and finished examples, then allow autonomous production and evolution. Use capable SaaS workflows as quality and functionality references for image ads, avatar/video ads and storefront creation.

Own the interface, data and workflows while using external SaaS or generation engines when they perform better. Evaluate documented APIs and the ability to return usable data to the system rather than rebuilding underlying AI models.

Supplier, 3PL and back-office automation is secondary. Include the basic supplier, cost and order information needed for product tests. A separate ERP, warehouse, accounting, support or retention suite is not required for the current delivery.
Private supplier discovery and negotiation remain possible later work, not mandatory acceptance for the current research, creative and testing delivery.
Dropshipping, bulk/private-label purchasing and 3PL are business context for testing and scaling. Comprehensive integration is secondary and requires an agreed scope.

Aim for autonomous execution. The main practical obstacle to solve is poor creative quality: use relevant competitor and customer language, strong product-specific copy and real evidence without turning ordinary work into repetitive approval paperwork.
Run product discovery and profitable scaling together, allowing investment in learning while expanding successful products.

The initial monthly business target is 60 product tests, at least two or three products suitable for scaling, and a majority reaching break-even through iteration. These are desired outcomes, not guaranteed software results.
An early tentative testing-budget suggestion was discussed and subsequently withdrawn as a design constraint.
The developer should recommend realistic resource requirements and economics rather than constrain the design to the earlier budget suggestion.

requirements.summary: The developer chooses the architecture. Repository content is methodology reference only, not a working codebase or a promise of reusable software.

Make the repository useful to a developer and coding assistant through clear workflow explanations, requirement summaries, memory-derived lessons, JSON/schema examples and traceable technical references. A separate browser chat application is not required.

Job-posting drafting chats are supplementary, lower-priority context. An earlier exclusion of live Upwork work was superseded by the later request for an actual job posting; this repository provides the ready-to-post hiring copy.

Present owner intent as clear assistant-written summaries instead of word-for-word quotations. Use a private GitHub repository as the primary developer handoff. The latest SaaS names supplied are amboris and arcads; Amboras is a likely match for the intended storefront platform, pending confirmation, while Arcads provides ad/video/avatar capabilities.
requirements.status: Historical repository-privacy preference; this developer repository is PUBLIC. All additions must remain public-safe.

requirements.summary: Current commercial position: $6,000-$8,000 negotiable fixed fee, with $8,000 as a ceiling rather than a committed price. Aim for about one month with access ready. Price, milestones and schedule must be agreed before hiring. Deliver connected research, finished creative, stores and campaign testing; secondary supplier/3PL/back-office systems are not mandatory acceptance.

Run the engine on Codex and Claude subscriptions through officially supported access. Limit paid API usage to video generation. Do not depend on separately billed LLM, copywriting, image-generation or other API calls. Disclose hosting, storage and other non-API costs before contracting; no new spend is authorized.

The clients are engineers and use AI coding tools. The quote must reflect AI-assisted development and sensible component reuse rather than an all-custom-from-scratch estimate. Explain custom work, integration, creative finishing and testing; do not default to the budget ceiling. Keep short personal replies, relevant work and staged Loom requests.

Keep historical agent, creative and system documents as methodology reference. Their presence does not establish working software, reusable components or delivery-time savings. A source-family/revision inventory is not a count of failed full builds.

Make the methodology visible to developers: which data to scrape or collect, fields to preserve and evidence to cross-reference, product research, copywriting, video production and performance feedback. Use earlier workflows, agents and attributed course-derived summaries. Dropshipping, product research and high-converting store/ad experience are preferred.

Prefer a custom agent-led operating system over static automation chains. Remove stale automation exports from the current handoff unless they explain a useful methodology. Preserve research, before/after, AI UGC and node-based creative methods without prescribing n8n or other legacy orchestration. Deterministic execution primitives remain useful beneath agent decisions.

Future-proofing is mandatory acceptance: owner-controlled records and portable exports; replaceable models/runtimes/prompts/skills/agent stages; controls outside model instructions; repeatable output/cost/reliability comparisons; demonstrated replacement, workflow simplification and restore without losing history or repeating external actions. Avoid a universal agent framework or a promise of compatibility with every future model.

Primary delivery is product research, finished ads and stores, campaign testing and improvement. Supplier/3PL work is secondary. This supersedes the earlier requirement that all logistics and back-office functions be complete in the same contract.
The developer may quote down toward $6,000 within a $6,000-$8,000 negotiable range. No price, milestone, deadline, award or new spending is committed by postings or applicant replies.
Pixel and conversion-event setup is core, with event receipt, consent behavior, product/value fields and browser/server deduplication verified against test orders.

Shopify store catalog creation and management at scale is core: products, variants, collections, copy, media and bulk updates, with draft review, stable IDs, item-level errors and duplicate-safe retries.

Provide visual product summaries for scraped products, landing pages and competitor ads, with images/previews, prices, source links/dates and concise assessments. The dashboard supports real research and execution rather than replacing them.

Include the upgrade demonstration and fixes needed to meet agreed acceptance in the negotiated build. Extra paid work requires written scope and price approval before starting. AI coding productivity should reduce implementation effort, not excuse untested outputs; price optional later maintenance separately.

Include WinningHunter, Kalodata, Atria, Brandsearch and Higgsfield as sourced capability/methodology references for product/ad/landing-page research, creative analytics, skills/workflows and reference-led original ads/pages. Do not require all subscriptions or claim current integrated capability from vendor documentation.

The system must retain and reuse ad-performance evidence to improve future briefs and variants, with reference-to-output comparisons and portable history. Distinguish vendor training claims, application learning through records/retrieval and actual model-weight training. Existing rights, supported access and video-only paid-API limits remain.
